principles.statement: Capture the learner's own first written response before exposing a full target model, translation, sentence rewrite or AI-generated answer whenever the task is intended to measure productive writing.
Separate communicative message success from lexical retrieval, construction use, organization, linguistic accuracy and mechanics instead of using one undifferentiated writing score.
Preserve planning, first-draft production and revision as separate writing-process evidence because instructional conditions can affect them and their outcomes differently.

Progress writing from bounded reconstruction to guided sentence generation, changed-content independent sentences, connected micro-writing and short functional writing by gradually increasing generative demand and reducing support.
Judge feedback by whether it improves later new writing, not only whether it improves the current corrected draft.
When learner history suggests a target form is already available, use a bounded retrieval/self-repair cue before supplying the corrected form.
When the needed form is unavailable or repeated self-repair fails, provide bounded positive evidence or direct correction rather than forcing unproductive guessing.
Prioritize a small set of high-value writing problems—message blocking, current targets and recurrent high-frequency errors—rather than correcting every surface error by default.
Use model texts primarily as post-draft comparators: establish learner ownership first, then provide positive evidence for noticing and comparison.
After comparator/model exposure, remove the model and require revision or new-content production so copying is distinguishable from retained language use.
Do not let AI or automated tools rewrite the target response before independent evidence capture when the educational objective is learner-generated writing.

Record the provenance and strength of every automated writing intervention, including hints, alternatives, direct corrections and rewrites, because resulting text quality has different evidential value at different support levels.
Store same-draft revision, immediate new-task transfer and delayed new-task writing as separate outcomes; never promote revised-draft quality directly to independent mastery.
Require delayed unsupported writing on unseen/new content before treating a writing capability or target construction as retained and independently usable.

Use automated feedback as an adjunct with confidence and scope gates, especially for near-A0 learners; do not present uncertain machine judgments or unvalidated holistic scores as objective writing ability.

Keep sentence-frame fading, micro-writing length, feedback scope, prompt-versus-correction policy, model timing, AI/AWE assistance limits, revision dose and delayed-transfer thresholds falsifiable until EXP-014 validates them with Vietnamese near-A0 learners.
